title: Toward the Treatment of Glioblastoma Tumors Using Photoactivated Chemotherapy: In Vitro Evaluation of Efficacy and Safety.
summary: This study evaluates ruthenium-based photoactivated chemotherapy (PACT) prodrugs in glioblastoma U-87MG cells and neuron-like SH-SY5Y cells, identifying [3](PF6)2 as a light-activated compound with improved anticancer efficacy (PI≈3.5) in GBM while showing reduced or reversed toxicity in SH-SY5Y upon green light exposure. Light-activated [3](PF6)2 markedly increased intracellular Ca2+ in SH-SY5Y cells, and docking suggested possible interaction with AMPA receptors, indicating promise for GBM treatment with attention to neuro-safety and calcium signaling.

title: A workflow integrating organ-on-chip culture and correlative 3D light and electron microscopy for microtissue analysis.
summary: The study presents a practical workflow that integrates organ-on-chip culture with longitudinal live fluorescence imaging and correlative 3D electron microscopy via high-pressure freezing to analyze microtissues at multiple scales. Demonstrated on an hMSC-derived bone-on-a-chip, the pipeline enables fluorescence-guided targeting for FIB/SEM and Raman characterization while supporting fluid flow and mechanical compression to model physiologic cues.

title: Distinct stromal cell populations define the B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia microenvironment.
crm_level_3: Princess Máxima Center for Pediatric Oncology
summary: This study maps the pediatric B-ALL bone marrow microenvironment at single-cell resolution and identifies two major stromal MSC populations—early mesenchymal progenitors and adipogenic progenitors—along with osteogenic-lineage cells detected by spatial transcriptomics. Functionally, adipogenic progenitors uniquely support leukemic cells via IL-7 and VCAM1 signaling and are enriched at relapse, while B-ALL cells drive a contact-dependent adipogenic skew in MSCs, highlighting stromal niche heterogeneity as a contributor to leukemic survival and chemoresistance.

title: NAD-dependent dehydrogenases enable efficient growth of Paracoccus denitrificans on the PET monomer ethylene glycol.
summary: The study identifies and characterizes an NAD-dependent alcohol dehydrogenase (EtgB) and aldehyde dehydrogenase (EtgA) in Paracoccus denitrificans that together enable efficient growth on the PET monomer ethylene glycol, under control of the activator EtgR. Structural (cryo-EM) and functional analyses, along with adaptive laboratory evolution, show increased EtgB/EtgA production accelerates ethylene glycol growth, and that the etg gene cluster is widespread across bacteria.

title: BDH2-driven lysosome-to-mitochondria iron transfer shapes ferroptosis vulnerability of the melanoma cell states.
summary: This study identifies BDH2 as a critical effector of lysosome-to-mitochondria Fe(II) transfer at mitochondria–lysosome contacts in melanoma, where it produces the siderophore 2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid (2,5-DHBA) to support mitochondrial bioenergetics, maintain lysosomal acidification, and stabilize contact formation. Loss of BDH2 in mesenchymal-like melanoma causes lysosomal iron sequestration and ferroptosis vulnerability, which can be mitigated by BDH2 re-expression or 2,5-DHBA, including improved metastatic seeding in vivo.

title: Modulation of immunoglobulin G oligomerization by variable domain glycans: A mechanism to regulate complement activation.
summary: This study shows that variable domain glycans (VDGs) on IgG inhibit classical complement activation by impeding IgG oligomerization into hexamers, thereby reducing C1q recruitment. Using glycoengineered human monoclonal antibodies, biochemical assays, and cryo-electron tomography, the authors demonstrate fewer, less-ordered IgG–C1 complexes and diminished complement-mediated membrane lysis when VDGs are present, revealing a regulatory mechanism that diversifies antibody effector function.

title: Long-term multi-meta-omics resolves the ecophysiological controls of seasonal N2O emissions during wastewater treatment.
summary: This study combined nearly two years of metagenome-resolved metaproteomics, ex situ kinetics, and full-scale operation data from a wastewater treatment plant to resolve the mechanistic drivers of seasonal nitrous oxide emissions. It shows that an oxygen- and temperature-driven imbalance between ammonia- and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria leads to nitrite build-up and overexpression of nitrifier denitrification (notably NirK), identifying dissolved oxygen control as the key lever to mitigate N2O peaks.

title: Protocol for generation of a 3D humanized lung-tumor-on-a-chip model of immune-hot and immune-cold microenvironments.
summary: This protocol describes a fully humanized lung tumor-on-a-chip model using Emulate’s Chip-S1 to recreate immune-hot (H2009) and immune-cold (A549) tumor microenvironments with human lung microvascular endothelial cells and perfused human PBMCs under controlled flow. It details setup, perfusion, imaging, immune infiltration analyses (IF, flow cytometry), and secretome profiling, and provides troubleshooting and limitations for reproducing dynamic endothelium–immune–tumor interactions.

title: CIP2A mediates mitotic recruitment of SLX4/MUS81/XPF to resolve replication stress-induced DNA lesions.
summary: This study shows that the mitotic CIP2A–TOPBP1 complex forms large filamentous and loop-like structures at sites of under-replicated DNA and recruits the SMX tri-nuclease complex (SLX4, MUS81, XPF–ERCC1) to process replication stress–induced DNA lesions, while being dispensable for mitotic DNA synthesis (MiDAS). The unstructured C-terminal tail of CIP2A is essential for higher-order structure formation and SMX recruitment; its loss increases genome instability and is synthetically lethal in BRCA2-deficient cells, with SLX4 loss phenocopying CIP2A loss in BRCA-deficient contexts.

title: High-resolution multi-omics enhances prediction and detection of smORF-encoded proteins in the human gut microbiome.
summary: This study introduces a high-resolution multi-omics workflow that integrates smORF prediction into sample-specific metaproteomic databases and leverages next-generation Orbitrap Astral mass spectrometry to detect small open reading frame-encoded proteins (SEPs) in human gut microbiomes without size-based enrichment. Applying the pipeline to healthy human stool samples yielded over 3.7 million non-redundant predicted smORFs and 25,233 detected SEPs, substantially expanding the experimentally supported small-protein landscape and aligning their taxonomic and functional profiles with the broader metaproteome.

title: Co-trimoxazole-induced reproductive toxicity and placental-barrier disruption: impact on cell-cell junctions and ERK signaling pathway.
summary: This study shows that co-trimoxazole (sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim) causes reproductive toxicity in pregnant mice and disrupts placental barrier function in vitro by altering tight/adherens junction gene expression, reducing TEER, increasing FITC-dextran permeability, activating ERK1/2, and suppressing IL-6. Findings indicate potential risks to placental integrity and fetal outcomes during CTX exposure, warranting careful risk-benefit evaluation in pregnancy.

title: Native long-read RNA sequencing of human monocytes reveals activation-induced alternative splicing toward functional isoforms.
summary: The study uses Oxford Nanopore native RNA sequencing to profile full-length isoforms in primary human monocytes before and after LPS activation, identifying over 24,000 isoforms with many novel variants and widespread activation-induced isoform switching. Activation favors longer, coding-competent isoforms with fewer retained introns, which correlate with increased translation and protein abundance, highlighting alternative splicing as a functional regulator of monocyte activation.

title: Constitutive activity of an atypical chemokine receptor revealed by inverse agonistic nanobodies.
summary: This study identifies inverse agonistic nanobodies (VUN700 and VUN702) that suppress the constitutive activity of the atypical chemokine receptor ACKR3, reducing basal β-arrestin engagement, inhibiting constitutive internalization, and slowing non-chemotactic cancer cell motility. Hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry and solution NMR show these nanobodies stabilize a more inactive receptor conformation than a neutral antagonist nanobody (VUN701), providing mechanistic insight and potential therapeutic strategies for ACKR3-driven pathophysiology.

title: Akkermansia muciniphila MucT harnesses dietary polyphenols as xenosiderophores for enhanced iron uptake.
summary: The study shows that Akkermansia muciniphila MucT exploits dietary proanthocyanidins (PACs) as xenosiderophores to import iron, upregulating a ferric catecholate ABC transporter (YclNOPQ), lipocalins, and ferrous iron transporters (Feo) and thereby restoring growth in iron-depleted conditions when supplied with iron-loaded PACs. Integrative proteomics/transcriptomics and iron-depletion assays implicate Fur and a DtxR-like regulator in coordinating these iron-acquisition systems, providing a mechanistic basis for PAC-driven enrichment of A. muciniphila and potential competitive advantages over pathogens.

title: Tractable mouse TNBC models capture the heterogeneous tumor immune microenvironment and adaptation to PD-L1 blockade.
summary: The study characterizes nine intraductal, syngeneic mouse triple-negative breast cancer models that span ‘hot’ to ‘cold’ tumor immune microenvironments and recapitulate growth, metastasis, and immune heterogeneity. Despite high PD-L1, both 4T1-hot and 4T1-cold models were resistant to PD-L1 blockade, adapting via increased CXCL10+ tumor-associated macrophages (cold) and cancer-associated fibroblasts (hot), highlighting cell-type–specific resistance mechanisms and therapeutic targets.

title: A model of Notch signalling control of angiogenesis: Evidence of a role for Notch ligand heterodimerization.
summary: This study combines biochemical experiments and mathematical modeling to show that JAG1 and DLL4 can form heterodimers that block DLL4-driven cis-inhibition of Notch1, while DLL4 (but not JAG1) efficiently trans-activates Notch1, thereby explaining the opposing roles of these ligands in angiogenic sprouting. The resulting model reproduces tip/stalk patterning in angiogenesis and predicts that DLL4–JAG1 heterodimerization together with ligand-specific affinities for Notch1 are critical determinants of endothelial cell fate.

title: Ethnomedicinal documentation, phytochemical characterization, and biological evaluation of the traditional medicinal plants from Swat region of Pakistan.
summary: This study documents ethnomedicinal uses, phytochemical profiles, TLC fingerprints, and a broad antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and cytotoxicity evaluation of 85 extracts from 17 traditional medicinal plants collected in the Swat region of Pakistan. Many extracts, especially ethanol extracts, showed substantial activity against planktonic bacteria and fungi and against biofilms (notably Staphylococcus aureus and Candida albicans) with generally low cytotoxicity, highlighting plants such as Juglans regia, Punica granatum, Artemisia maritima, Aesculus indica, Thymus linearis, Dysphania ambrosioides, and Nasturtium officinale as promising for further drug discovery work.

title: Ferroptosis inhibition protects against α-synuclein-related neuronal cell death.
summary: This study links α-synuclein pathology in Parkinson’s disease to increased ferroptosis vulnerability by showing reduced ferritin and ferroportin in α-syn-positive dopaminergic neurons, ferroptosis-related transcriptomic changes in substantia nigra, and enhanced neuronal death when α-syn fibrils are combined with the GPX4 inhibitor RSL3. Ferroptosis inhibition with ferrostatin-1 (but not deferoxamine) protected mouse primary cortical neurons and human LUHMES dopaminergic neurons, and iron chelation reduced α-syn inclusions in C. elegans, supporting ferroptosis as a therapeutic target, albeit with cell- and model-dependent effects.

title: The complexome contextualizes proteomics data to fingerprint biological states and highlight perturbed functional modules in disease.
summary: This study introduces a complexome-centered framework and software (ComplexomeProfiler) that overlays proteomics measurements onto curated protein complexes to fingerprint biological states and detect perturbed functional modules. Benchmarking across human tissues (PaxDb) and analyzing proteomes from patient-derived fibroblasts with inborn errors of metabolism revealed consistent remodeling of mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and broader mitochondrial machinery, providing mechanistic insights into disease states.

title: Cryo-EM analysis of the Bacillus thuringiensis extrasporal matrix identifies F-ENA as a widespread family of endospore appendages across the Firmicutes phylum
summary: This study identifies and structurally characterizes a new family of endospore appendages (F-ENA) across Firmicutes, showing that Bacillus thuringiensis spores display flexible DUF4183-based pili tethered to the exosporium by a collagen-like F-Anchor and capped by a collagen-like F-BclA fibrillum. Using cryo-EM, crystallography and AlphaFold modeling, the authors define F-ENA architecture and assembly, document variants in Paenibacillus and Clostridia, and show F-ENA contributes to spore clustering.

title: The lipid transfer protein STARD7 controls intestinal tumor development in a context-dependent manner.
summary: This study shows that loss of the phosphatidylcholine transfer protein STARD7 in intestinal epithelial cells causes mitochondrial stress, elevated ROS, and mTORC1/ATF4-driven metabolic reprogramming, notably upregulating serine biosynthesis. Functionally, STARD7 deficiency reduces inflammation-driven (AOM/DSS) colon tumors but accelerates Wnt-driven tumor initiation in Apc+/Min mice via increased mutation burden and a microbiota shift, and these tumors are highly sensitive to mTORC1 inhibition (rapamycin).

title: Inhibitor-based modulation of huntingtin aggregation mechanisms mitigates fibril-induced cellular stress.
summary: This study shows that sub-stoichiometric curcumin modulates huntingtin exon 1 (HttEx1) aggregation by prolonging the nucleation lag phase and yielding narrower amyloid fibril polymorphs with altered morphology and dynamics. These curcumin-induced fibrils provoke reduced cellular stress in neuronal models, with structural changes supported by TEM, SAXS, and solid-state NMR consistent with differences in polyglutamine core organization and flanking-domain dynamics.

title: Dual NIR-I excitation and emission-based thermometry and pH-responsive drug delivery using NaYF4:Yb,Er@SiO2-folic acid conjugates.
summary: The authors synthesize cuboidal NaYF4:Yb,Er upconverting particles, coat them with mesoporous silica, conjugate folic acid, and load doxorubicin to create a theranostic platform that enables dual NIR-I excitation/emission ratiometric thermometry and pH-responsive drug delivery. They demonstrate stable temperature sensing in water and through chicken breast tissue under 975/940 nm excitation, quantify DOX loading/release and cytotoxicity, and show preferential anticancer effects in HeLa cells while maintaining good biocompatibility in NHDFs.

title: A group 1 hemagglutinin stem vaccine elicits broad humoral responses against influenza in phase 1/2a study.
summary: This randomized, double-blind Phase 1/2a trial tested a soluble trimeric group 1 hemagglutinin stem protein (INFLUENZA G1 mHA) in healthy adults, showing it was well tolerated and induced markedly higher, broader, and durable binding, neutralizing, and ADCC antibody responses than a standard quadrivalent seasonal influenza vaccine. Vaccinee sera conferred significant protection in a stringent H5N1 passive-transfer mouse challenge, supporting the HA-stem approach as a component toward a universal influenza vaccine.

title: Characterizing the Fate of Anti-CS1 Nanobody Displaying Extracellular Vesicles in Multiple Myeloma.
summary: The study engineered HEK293-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) to display anti-CS1 nanobodies to target multiple myeloma (MM) and evaluated their biodistribution and cellular uptake in vitro and in vivo. While α-CS1 EVs enhanced uptake by CS1+ myeloma cells in vitro, in vivo they showed only modest bone marrow retention with increased off-target accumulation (notably liver and lungs) and no improved specificity for MM cells in diseased mice, indicating further optimization is required for targeted EV delivery in MM.

title: Intestinal tuft cell subtypes represent successive stages of maturation driven by crypt-villus signaling gradients.
summary: This study shows that intestinal tuft-1 and tuft-2 cells are not distinct endpoints but successive post-mitotic maturation states along the crypt–villus axis, with chemosensory capacity increasing during maturation. Using mouse small-intestinal organoids with subtype-specific reporters, the authors demonstrate that IL-4/IL-13 generate new Nrep+ tuft-1 cells, while villus-like cues (notably BMPs and cholinergic signaling) drive their progression to Chat+/Folr1+ tuft-2 cells, enabling functional assays of mature tuft cells.

title: Macrophage-augmented intestinal organoids model virus-host interactions in enteric viral diseases and facilitate therapeutic development.
summary: This study develops macrophage-augmented intestinal organoids (MaugOs) by integrating human macrophages with primary human intestinal organoids to model enteric virus–host interactions, showing differential antiviral and inflammatory responses to echoviruses, rotavirus, OC43, and SARS-CoV-2. The authors demonstrate that acetate potently suppresses NLRP3-driven inflammation and that combining the antiviral nirmatrelvir with either budesonide or acetate concurrently reduces viral replication and inflammatory responses in MaugOs.

title: Pharmacological CLK inhibition disrupts SR protein function and RNA splicing blocking cell growth and migration in TNBC.
summary: This study demonstrates that the CLK inhibitor T-025 disrupts SR protein function and RNA splicing, leading to impaired proliferation, G1–S arrest with increased 4N DNA content and aneuploidy, and reduced migration in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) cell lines. Mechanistically, T-025 causes SR factors (notably SRSF7) to accumulate and interact within nuclear speckles, alters SRSF7’s interactome, and reprograms alternative splicing across genes governing cell division and migration.

title: Cryo-EM identifies F-ENA of Bacillus thuringiensis as a widespread family of endospore appendages across Firmicutes.
summary: This study identifies and structurally characterizes a new family of endospore appendages, F-ENA, across Firmicutes, showing they are DUF4183-based, C3-symmetric pili tethered to the exosporium via a collagen-like F-Anchor and capped by a collagen-like tip fibrillum (F-BclA). Using cryo-EM, X-ray crystallography, and proteomics, the authors reveal F-ENA promotes spore clustering, is widespread in Bacilli and Clostridia, and exhibits subgroup-specific neck domains that modulate filament architecture.

title: Epithelial Cell Mechanoresponse to Matrix Viscoelasticity and Confinement Within Micropatterned Viscoelastic Hydrogels.
summary: The authors developed micropatterned viscoelastic polyacrylamide hydrogels with independently tunable stiffness and stress relaxation to mimic the mechanical evolution of breast tissue from soft viscoelastic to stiff elastic states, and showed that viscoelasticity differentially regulates epithelial cell spreading, focal adhesions, YAP nuclear localization, and migration depending on initial stiffness. Spatial confinement on 1D fibronectin lines altered these viscoelasticity-driven responses, enhancing or suppressing migration via changes in actin retrograde flow and adhesion dynamics, and generally blunting viscoelastic effects under confinement on soft matrices.

title: Co-translational protein aggregation and ribosome stalling as a broad-spectrum antibacterial mechanism.
crm_level_1: VIB Center for Brain and Disease Research
crm_level_3: VIB Center for Brain and Disease Research
summary: The study introduces an aggregation‑prone peptide (P33) that penetrates bacteria without disrupting membranes, induces co‑translational aggregation of nascent polypeptides, traps stalled ribosomes and cognate mRNAs in inclusion bodies, and thereby kills a broad spectrum of ESKAPE pathogens, including in biofilms and in mouse infection models. Multi-omics and imaging show inclusion bodies enriched for ribosomal components and outer membrane proteins, while inhibition of translation (erythromycin) abrogates aggregation and lethality, supporting a mechanism of ribosome stalling via nascent chain aggregation.

title: Illuminating Rembrandt's Chiaroscuro in The Night Watch: the painting process of Van Ruytenburch's costume.
summary: Using noninvasive chemical imaging (MA-XRF, MA-XRPD, and RIS), microscopy, and targeted micro-sampling, the study maps Rembrandt’s pigment choices and layer structure to explain the chiaroscuro rendering of Lieutenant Van Ruytenburch’s costume in The Night Watch. It reveals systematic pigment groupings (e.g., lead white and lead–tin yellow impastos, smalt-enriched underpaints, arsenic-based pigments for golden reflections) and documents degradation products (mimetite, palmierite, weddellite) that now mute the original light–shadow effects and inform conservation strategy.

title: Evidence That Dmrta2 Acts through Repression of Pax6 in Cortical Patterning and Identification of a Mutation Impairing DNA Recognition Associated with Microcephaly in Human.
summary: This study demonstrates that Dmrta2 represses Pax6 to control cortical patterning and cooperate with Pax6 to maintain dorsal telencephalic identity, with genetic interactions shown by double mutant and double overexpression mouse models. Mechanistically, Dmrta2 represses Pax6 E60 enhancer activity in a DNA-binding dependent manner, recruits NuRD components (HDAC1/2, MBD3) potentially via Zfp423, and a human DMRTA2 p.Arg116Pro mutation that abolishes DNA binding is associated with microcephaly and corpus callosum agenesis.

title: The Escherichia coli replication initiator DnaA is titrated on the chromosome.
summary: This study combines genome-wide motif analysis and live-cell single-particle tracking to show that Escherichia coli chromosomes enrich high-affinity DnaA-binding sites near oriC and titrate DnaA in a growth rate-dependent manner, keeping a large fraction of DnaA DNA-bound especially during slow growth. Deleting datA, DARS1, and DARS2 reduces chromosomal titration capacity in slow growth, increases DnaA mobility, and leads to premature re-initiation events, indicating that titration stabilizes replication initiation by limiting free DnaA after initiation.

title: Traction Force Microscopy for Viscoelastic Substrates: A Semi-Analytical Method.
summary: The study introduces a semi-analytical, time-resolved viscoelastic traction force microscopy (veTFM) method that generalizes standard 2D elastic TFM to linear Generalized Maxwell substrates, enabling fast, Fourier–Laplace-based inversion of interfacial displacements to tractions while accounting for dissipation and finite thickness. Validated against analytical and FEM solutions and applied to human cardiomyocytes, mammary epithelial cells, and dermal fibroblasts on linear-polyacrylamide and alginate hydrogels, veTFM shows when elastic limits suffice and reveals that traction magnitudes scale primarily with total substrate dissipation, with timescale matching determining whether cells engage elastic or viscoelastic regimes.

title: A coronavirus assembly inhibitor that targets the viral membrane protein.
summary: This study reports the discovery of CIM-834, a small-molecule inhibitor that targets the coronavirus membrane (M) protein and blocks the conformational switch required for virion assembly, thereby potently inhibiting SARS-CoV-2 (multiple variants) and SARS-CoV in cells and in vivo. Structural, biochemical, and electron microscopy data show CIM-834 binds and stabilizes the short form of M, abolishing particle assembly, reducing lung viral titers in SCID mice and Syrian hamsters, and preventing transmission in hamsters.

title: WEE1 inhibitors trigger GCN2-mediated activation of the integrated stress response.
summary: The study shows that clinically used WEE1 inhibitors (AZD1775 and Debio 0123) activate the GCN2-dependent integrated stress response (ISR), causing global translational attenuation and that loss of ISR components (GCN2/GCN1/ATF4) reduces WEE1i cytotoxicity without preventing WEE1i-induced DNA damage or checkpoint override. ISR activation appears to be an off-target effect common to multiple WEE1 inhibitors and occurs in primary human PBMCs; importantly, low-dose WEE1 inhibition combined with PKMYT1 inhibition maintains antitumor synergy without inducing the ISR.

title: Recombinant Proteins: A Molecular Tool to Understand Marine Adhesion and to Advance Biomaterials.
summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge on recombinant proteins that mimic marine invertebrate adhesives (mussels, scallops, barnacles, tubeworms, ascidians, sea anemones, sea stars), covering their identification, recombinant production across host systems, functional characterization, hybrid protein design, and translation into biomaterials. It highlights production hurdles (PTMs, inclusion bodies), enzymatic post-processing (tyrosinase), domain-focused truncations, and the creation of coacervates, hydrogels, fibers, and coatings for biomedical applications.

title: Clathrin-independent endocytosis and retrograde transport in cancer cells tune immune synapse organization and CD8 T cell response.
summary: This study identifies ICAM1 as a new cargo of Endophilin A3–mediated clathrin‑independent endocytosis in cancer cells and shows that, together with ALCAM, it undergoes retromer‑dependent retrograde transport to the trans‑Golgi network before polarized delivery to the immune synapse. Disrupting EndoA3 or retromer reduces CD8 T‑cell cytokine production but increases lytic activity and enlarges immune synapses, indicating altered synapse organization and a shift toward more transient, serial killing interactions.

title: In silico analysis of patient specific coagulation and flow effects on fibrin clot formation.
summary: This study presents a unified, assay-calibrated in silico framework that links patient-specific thrombin generation (TG) data to multi-dimensional coagulation simulations under flow in patient-specific vascular geometries. The model, validated against thrombodynamics (TD) outcomes, shows how plasma composition, tissue factor (TF) exposure, and hemodynamics jointly modulate fibrin formation, enabling individualized assessment of thrombotic potential.

title: Enhancer-driven cell type comparison reveals similarities between the mammalian and bird pallium.
crm_level_1: VIB Center for AI & Computational Biology
summary: The study generated single-cell multiome and spatial transcriptomics datasets of the chicken telencephalon and trained cross-species deep learning models on cell type–specific accessible chromatin to decode enhancer codes that define cell identities. They found highly conserved enhancer codes across birds and mammals for non-neuronal and GABAergic neurons, while excitatory neurons showed mixed 1:many correspondences, and validated predicted enhancers in vitro (MPRA) and in vivo (AAV reporter assays).

title: Reprogramming the EnvZ-OmpR two-component system confers ethanol tolerance in Escherichia coli by stabilizing the outer membrane and altering ferric homeostasis.
crm_level_3: Centre of Microbial and Plant Genetics (Department of Molecular and Microbial Systems)
summary: This study shows that a single EnvZ periplasmic-domain mutation (L116P) in Escherichia coli reprograms the EnvZ-OmpR two‑component system into a kinase-dominant state, stabilizing the outer membrane by elevating total OmpC/OmpF porin abundance and decreasing ferric uptake via repression of enterobactin biosynthesis and ferric transport. The mutation confers strong ethanol tolerance and boosts ethanol production rates, with TolC and LpcA essential for the tolerant phenotype, while providing no cross-tolerance to n-propanol or n-butanol.

title: Leveraging Targeted Protein Degradation for G Protein-Coupled Receptors: The Development of CCR2 Molecular Degraders.
summary: The study develops and validates the first small-molecule molecular degraders of the GPCR CCR2 by tethering an intracellular allosteric CCR2 ligand to E3 ligase recruiters, identifying CRBN-recruiting compounds (notably LUF7996) that induce potent, sustained CCR2 degradation. Mechanistic profiling shows degradation proceeds via a lysosomal pathway (not proteasomal), and the lead degrader inhibits CCR2-dependent monocyte migration in THP-1 cells, establishing a workflow to expand GPCR-targeted degradation.

title: Peptidomimetic Phenoxymethyl Ketone Warheads as Potent Dual-Mode Inhibitors against SARS-CoV-2 Mpro and Cathepsin.
summary: This study reports a library of peptidomimetic phenoxymethyl ketone (PMK) inhibitors that act dually on SARS‑CoV‑2 main protease (Mpro) and host cathepsins (hCTSL/hCTSB), showing nanomolar biochemical potency, robust cellular antiviral activity, and broad-spectrum efficacy against SARS‑CoV and MERS‑CoV. Lead compound 1 demonstrated favorable in vivo plasma exposure in Syrian golden hamsters (with ritonavir coadministration), while ADME profiling highlighted fast hepatic clearance mitigated by CYP3A4 inhibition, supporting advancement to in vivo efficacy studies.

title: Pre-assembly of biomolecular condensate seeds drives RSV replication.
summary: This study reveals that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) nucleates its viral factories (biomolecular condensates) from infecting viral ribonucleoproteins (vRNPs) that already carry pre-assembled protein interaction networks, termed pre-replication centres (PRCs). Using live single-vRNP imaging tools, the authors show PRCs are enriched for P and L, highly transcriptionally active, recruit viral proteins efficiently, and thus seed rapid viral factory formation, explaining infection heterogeneity by virion-to-virion variation in PRC content.

title: A scalable tumor-vasculature-on-chip for CAR T cell trafficking and efficacy studies
authors: De Haan, Luuk; Olczyk, Aleksandra; Olivier, Thomas; Wesselius, Joris; Suijker, Johnny; Al-Mardini, Claudia; Burton, Todd; Van Den Broek, Lenie; Queiroz, Karla

summary: The study presents a scalable tumor-vasculature-on-chip model (OrganoPlate) that enables quantification of CAR T cell extravasation, infiltration, target recognition, killing, and cytokine release against 3D ECM-embedded tumor cells adjacent to a perfused endothelial vessel. EpCAM-targeting CAR T cells specifically eliminated EpCAM+ HT-29 but not EpCAM− A375 cells in an E:T ratio- and IL-2–dependent manner, disrupted endothelium at high doses, distinguished CD28 vs 4-1BB CAR designs, and supported testing of checkpoint inhibitors and temozolomide.
summary_mandm: Human tumor cell lines (HT-29-GFP, A375-GFP, HCT116-GFP) were maintained in DMEM or RPMI-1640 with FBS, L-glutamine, and Pen/Strep, with G418 or puromycin selection after thaw; HUVECs were cultured in EGM-2, and CAR T cells (EpCAM scFv-CD28-CD3ζ and EpCAM scFv-4-1BB-CD3ζ) were expanded per vendor or thawed and recovered in AIM-V. Tumor cells were harvested with 0.025% trypsin/EDTA (Lonza), counted, and embedded at 5.7e6 cells/mL in an ECM composed of collagen I (final 3.6 mg/mL) and fibronectin (0.1 mg/mL) prepared by mixing collagen I:HEPES:NaHCO3 at 8:1:1, then polymerized 12 minutes at 37 °C/5% CO2 before adding AIM-V. HUVECs (2 µL at 1e7 cells/mL) were loaded into the top channel of the OrganoPlate 3-lane 40, attached 2 hours in a plate stand, and perfused on an OrganoFlow rocker (7°, 8-minute interval) for 4 days to form a vessel; endothelium was activated with TNFα 4 ng/mL for 4 hours before adding CAR T cells. CAR T cells were optionally labeled with DiR (0.5 µM, 20 minutes at 37 °C), resuspended to 5.7e5 cells/mL, and introduced apically at defined E:T ratios (1:2 to 10:1); IL-2 (50 IU/mL) or chemokine CXCL12 (800 ng/mL) was added as indicated, and checkpoint inhibitors (Nivolumab, Ipilimumab) and Temozolomide were dosed to specified final concentrations. Co-cultures were monitored 24–72 hours by spinning-disk confocal imaging, cytokines quantified by Luminex, and endpoint fixation used 3.7% formaldehyde followed by ICC for VE-cadherin and CD45; morphometrics were extracted using IN Carta.

title: Addition of DMSO to T cell cultures skews differentiation towards a memory phenotype
authors: De Bousser, Elien; Festjens, Nele; Plets, Evelyn; Meuris, Leander; Callewaert, Nico
journal: BioRxiv : the Preprint Server for Biology
raw_affiliation: Ghent University

summary: This study shows that adding low concentrations of DMSO (0.1–1.2% v/v) to human T cell cultures skews CD8+ and total CD3+ T cells toward memory phenotypes without compromising viability, with dose-dependent effects on activation and exhaustion markers (increased CD69, reduced TIM-3). The effect is observed across different cytokine conditions (IL-2 or IL-7/IL-15) and suggests potential utility for improving adoptive T cell therapies by enriching memory-like T cells during ex vivo expansion.
summary_mandm: Human leukocyte-enriched buffy coats were processed by Ficoll-Paque density centrifugation using Leucosep tubes to obtain peripheral blood lymphocytes; CD8+ or CD3+ T cells were isolated by magnetic negative selection (MojoSort kits). CD8+ T cells were cultured in RPMI 1640 with L-glutamine, 0.4 mM sodium pyruvate, 50 μM β-mercaptoethanol, and 10% heat-inactivated FCS; activated with anti-CD3/CD28 Dynabeads (1:3 bead:cell, 4 days, 37°C), beads removed by magnet, then cultured with IL-2 (50 U/mL) or IL-7 (10 ng/mL)/IL-15 (1 ng/mL). CD3+ T cells were cultured in IMDM + GlutaMAX with 10% FCS; activated with ImmunoCult Human CD3/CD28 T cell Activator (25 μL/10^6 cells, 3 days, 37°C) in the presence of IL-12 (10 ng/mL), then maintained with IL-7 (10 ng/mL) and IL-15 (10 ng/mL) at 1–3×10^6 cells/mL. DMSO (Sigma) at 0.1–1.2% v/v was added from day 0 and refreshed with cytokines/medium every 2–3 days (CD8+ protocol also refreshed on days 4/6/8/10); no enzymatic tissue digestion was used, and mechanical bead removal was performed with a magnet; proliferation was tracked with Tag-it Violet dye; flow cytometry was performed on a BD FACS Symphony.

Prior to cell seeding, cells were washed twice with PBS before putting them in culture with rhIL-7 at 10ng/mL (Miltenyi) and rhIL-15 at 10 ng/mL (Miltenyi).

title: Addressing clinical uncertainties in ATMP reimbursement: a review of methodological guidelines and European practice.
authors: Delemarre, Lotte; Huys, Isabelle; Van Dyck, Walter; Simoens, Steven

summary: This review examines how European health technology assessment guidelines and practices address key evidentiary uncertainties for Advanced Therapy Medicinal Products, focusing on indirect treatment comparisons and surrogate endpoints amid frequent reliance on single-arm trials and immature long-term outcomes. It highlights gaps and variability in guidance, evaluates emerging methods and innovative trial designs, and recommends lifecycle evidence generation to support more consistent reimbursement decisions.
summary_mandm: A narrative, structured literature review was conducted (Nov 2024–Feb 2025) using PubMed and Embase with predefined keywords (Health Technology Assessment; ATMP; Indirect Treatment Comparison; Surrogate Endpoint), supplemented by grey literature (HTA guidance, international organization reports) and the ISPOR pharmacoeconomic guideline database; snowballing of references enhanced completeness. Eligibility included English peer-reviewed reviews/document analyses and authoritative grey literature; screening (titles/abstracts, then full text) and selection were performed by one reviewer, data were charted for relevance to ITCs, surrogate endpoints, and innovative trial designs, European pharmacoeconomic guidelines were comparatively analyzed, and findings were synthesized narratively due to heterogeneity; no biological samples, digestions, enzymes, or mechanical processing were involved.

title: Advances in ex vivo mRNA-based gene transfer for cell-based cancer immunotherapy.
authors: Van Oers, Florian; Katana, Zoi; Flumens, Donovan; Lion, Eva; Campillo-Davo, Diana
citation: Mol Ther Nucleic Acids. 2026 Sep 8;37(3):102994. doi: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.omtn.2026.102994

summary: This review synthesizes advances in ex vivo mRNA electroporation as a non-integrating, transient gene transfer platform to engineer dendritic cells, T cells, NK cells, and B cells for cancer immunotherapy, covering both preclinical and early clinical experiences. It details applications such as DC antigen loading and maturation (TriMix/TetraMix), TCR and CAR redirection of T/NK cells, multiplex mRNA co-delivery (cytokines, chemokine receptors, adjuvants), and compares performance, safety, scheduling, and devices used across studies.
summary_mandm: Across the studies summarized, immune cells were engineered predominantly by ex vivo mRNA electroporation using square-wave or exponential-decay pulses on instruments such as BTX ECM830, Bio-Rad Gene Pulser/Gene Pulser Xcell/II, Lonza/Amaxa Nucleofector (2b/4D), MaxCyte GT/STx, NEPA21, Eppendorf Multiporator, AgilePulse MAX, and others; typical settings included 300–500 V, 0.5–5 ms (2–4 mm cuvettes), with 100–600 μL buffers and 10–100 μg mRNA (or μg/mL equivalents), with expression windows often assessed at 4–24 h. DCs were generated (commonly IL-4 DCs or IL-15 DCs) and matured either with cytokine cocktails (e.g., IFN-γ/TNF-α) or by co-electroporation of TriMix (CD70, CD40L, caTLR4) or TetraMix; NK cells were expanded with IL-15±IL-21 and/or feeder systems (e.g., K562 cells expressing membrane-bound cytokines/4-1BBL) and sometimes prestimulated 3 days with IL-15 before EP; T cells/PBMCs/PBLs were activated with anti-CD3 (OKT3) or CD3/CD28 Dynabeads prior to EP, with some protocols co-electroporating adjuvant mRNAs (e.g., IL-12, IL-15, IL-2, CXCR1/2/4/7, caTLR4, caCD40). No tissue digestion enzymology was described; instead, workflows focused on electroporation parameters, cytokine-driven culture/maturation, and timed incubations (e.g., avoiding 48 h DC maturation via TriMix, or weekly CAR-mRNA dosing schedules); mechanical processing devices beyond electroporators were not specified.

summary: ASS1-deficient cancer cells subjected to arginine deprivation undergo codon-biased mistranslation—most prominently +1 frameshifts at AGA codons driven by selective loss of tRNAArg(UCU) via METTL1/WDR4-dependent m7G46 modulation—resulting in aberrant proteins and shared HLA-presented neoepitopes. summary: The study introduces Bilayer Acoustic Force Spectroscopy (BAFS), which measures immune synapse binding strength by replacing target cells with antigen-functionalized supported lipid bilayers in a z-Movi acoustic force setup, thereby minimizing non-specific binding and dramatically improving signal-to-noise. BAFS reveals how CAR–CD19 synapse strength scales with antigen density and shows that CD8 synergistically enhances αβTCR–pMHC binding independently of Lck recruitment, demonstrating broad applicability for receptor screening and mechanistic dissection.

For BAFS, z‑Movi (LUMICKS) microfluidic chips were cleaned (Hellmanex, NaOH), then supported lipid bilayers were formed by incubating small unilamellar vesicles (DOPC with 1% DGS‑NTA(Ni) or 1% Biotin‑Cap‑PE; 0.2 mg/mL; ≥30 min) and passivated (0.5% casein or 5% BSA); bilayers were functionalized 1 h with His‑tag CD19 (0.314 μM) or HLA‑A*02:01 NY‑ESO‑1 9V single-chain trimer (100 nM), washed into imaging medium, and validated for fluidity by FRAP/TIRF. Effector cells (stained with CellTrace Far Red) were incubated on the bilayer for 5 min before an acoustic force ramp (0–1000 pN, 1.333 pN increments) detached cells for avidity readouts; ligand density was titrated by varying DGS‑NTA(Ni) from 1% to 0.01% or using biotin/NeutrAvidin chemistry. For cell-based AFS, PLL-coated chips were seeded with target cell monolayers (30 min), excess cells washed, and the same force protocol applied. summary: This retrospective descriptive analysis of 47 unsuccessful Article 8(3) EU centralized marketing authorization applications (2021–2025) found that clinical evidence deficiencies—especially inadequate study design and insufficient efficacy—were the most common drivers of both formal CHMP refusals and pre-opinion withdrawals. Withdrawn applications more often exhibited additional CMC and regulatory/procedural issues, and both withdrawals and refusals frequently exceeded EMA benchmark timelines largely due to prolonged clock-stop periods, underscoring the need for earlier cross-domain readiness assessment.
summary_mandm: The study performed a retrospective review of EMA public assessment documents (EPAR refusals, withdrawal Q&A) for Article 8(3) full-dossier MAAs from 2021–2025, filtered from the EMA Medicines Data Table (downloaded March 5, 2026), with supplementary dates from Citeline’s Pink Sheet, company reports, and press releases; 47 cases met inclusion after excluding veterinary products, duplicates, biosimilars, generics, and well-established use applications. A structured, binary scoring framework captured presence/absence of concerns across four domains—CMC, non-clinical, clinical, regulatory/procedural—with predefined secondary subcategories; procedural timelines were benchmarked to EMA guidance (full procedure ~349 days including validation, 90- and 30-day clock-stops; re-examination 120 days) and withdrawals were classified by phase based on Q&A wording (e.g., during initial evaluation, first clock-stop, Day 121–180, second clock-stop, Day 181–210). Data were extracted and coded in Microsoft Excel by two reviewers with consensus resolution; analyses were descriptive (counts, percentages, duration summaries) with figures generated in Excel/PowerPoint/BioRender and no inferential statistics. No biological sample preparation, digestion methods, enzymes, buffers, temperatures, incubation steps, or mechanical processing were involved.

title: Dewatering assessment of sewage sludge: a remaining challenge.
authors: Pavez-Jara, Javier; Korving, Leon; Jeison, David; De Kreuk, Merle K
journal: Reviews in Environmental Science and Bio/Technology
raw_affiliation: Department of Water Management, Delft University of Technology, Stevinweg 1, 2628 CN Delft, Delft, The Netherlands.
summary: This review critiques common laboratory indices for sewage sludge dewaterability (e.g., CST, sedimentation, SRF) for failing to predict full-scale performance because they overlook key phenomena—especially compression and expression—and identifies sludge compressibility as a critical factor. It links dewatering performance to four phenomena (mixing, destabilization, floc formation, compression/expression), recommends centrifugation, dead-end filtration, and combined centrifugation–filtration as better lab proxies, and calls for standardized, mechanistic methods to evaluate emerging eco-friendly conditioners.
summary_mandm: As a methods-focused review, it dissects dewatering into four operational stages—mixing (quantified by G·t: mean velocity gradient × time), suspension destabilization (assessed by zeta potential and streaming current nearing isoelectricity), floc formation (shear-sensitive growth/fragmentation), and compression/expression (governing final solids)—and maps these to laboratory assessments. It details capillary suction time (CST) using a standard column-on-filter-paper apparatus that measures radial drainage time and notes sensitivity to filter paper, temperature, solids, and geometry; sedimentation metrics SVI (30-minute settling) and ZSV for dilute matrices; centrifugation tests benchmarked by relative centrifugal force (RCF) and the composite RCF·t; a modified centrifugation–filtration setup (filter cloth partition in a spinning tube) that better emulates cake compaction; specific resistance to filtration (SRF) via vacuum-driven dead-end filtration (typical TMP ~50.7 kPa) using Darcy analysis (t/V vs V slope) with attention to cake compressibility and filter cloth pore size; and lab filter-press methods employing positive pressure and full-scale-like cloths to reach higher TMPs. It emphasizes matching lab conditions to practice (polymer dilution water quality, mixing intensity without polymer degradation, TMP/RCF and duration, filter cloth pore size) and notes operational covariates (e.g., pH, conductivity, divalent cations Ca2+/Mg2+, temperature influences on CST) while cautioning that many indices inadequately capture compression/expression, the dominant determinants of final cake solids.
instrument: capillary suction time (CST) apparatus with filter paper; laboratory centrifuge (RCF-based); modified centrifugation–filtration rig with filter cloth; vacuum filtration setup for SRF; plate/chamber filter press (positive-pressure dead-end filtration); belt filter press; decanter (solid bowl) centrifuge; streaming current detector; zeta potential analyzer; viscometer

summary: The authors introduce TWISTAR, a transcriptome-wide TCR deorphanization platform that screens single-cell–derived TCRs against autologous tumor cDNA libraries in HLA-engineered APCs to directly recover functionally immunogenic antigens. Applying TWISTAR to melanoma, breast, and HCC samples reveals a broad, shared antigen landscape dominated by non-canonical and tumor-associated targets, with convergent immune dominance across patients, informing pan-cancer vaccine design.
summary_mandm: Human TIL-derived TCRs and healthy donor PBMCs were used alongside tumor and HEK293T-derived cell lines; PBMCs were isolated from buffy coats by Ficoll density centrifugation (GE Healthcare #17-5442-02), cultured in IMDM with 10% FBS and supplements, and activated with T Cell TransAct (1:100, Miltenyi), then transduced by lentivirus via spinoculation (8 µg/mL polybrene, 800 × g, 45 min, 32°C), sorted by FACS, rested 5 days, and used in co-cultures. TWISTAR libraries were prepared from autologous tumor RNA using NEBNext Ultra II Directional RNA library prep with poly(A) selection and randomized fragmentation to ~300 bp inserts, cloned into a modified pLenti6.2 vector (mCherry-P2A-PuroR), transformed in Endura electrocompetent cells, and transduced into HLA-I-null 293T cells reconstituted with individual patient HLA alleles (and B2M/TAP1/TAPBP overexpression); Jurkat E6.1-based NFAT-GFP reporter cells were engineered by CRISPR/Cas9 knockout of endogenous TCRα/β (pX458) and CD8 expression, and TCRs were expressed from a pWPXL lentiviral backbone. Screening used automated microscopy to detect GFP+ T-cell clusters, followed by custom cell picking; peptide-HLA predictions (NetMHCpan) were validated by peptide-pulse assays (2 h peptide incubation at 37°C, wash, 24 h co-culture), and TrypLE was used to dissociate picked APCs; lytic assays used Incucyte S3 imaging (24–48 h co-cultures).

summary: The study introduces TCRPPO2, a reinforcement learning framework with a generative critic to optimize peptide-specific TCR sequences, and applies it to the MART-1 epitope to computationally design higher-affinity TCRs. Multiple engineered TCRs showed enhanced activity in Jurkat NFAT-reporter assays, with improvements supported by structural modeling, DSMBind and Rosetta energy scoring, and MD/MM/GBSA analyses.
summary_mandm: No tissue digestion was performed; experiments used human Jurkat CD8+ reporter cells and T2 APCs. TCR constructs were assembled into a pMXs-TCRβ-P2A-TCRα-IRES-puro retroviral vector using NEBuilder HiFi DNA Assembly Master Mix and Gibson Assembly, packaged in PhoenixGP-GaLV cells, used to transduce Jurkat CD8-J2 cells followed by puromycin selection (1 µg/mL); in parallel, TAP fragments (assembled TCR α/β with constant regions) and pGL4.30 NFAT-luciferase were electroporated into CD8-J2 cells using the Neon Electroporation System, and 5×10^4 CD8-J2-Luc-TCR cells were co-cultured overnight with 2×10^4 T2 cells and titrated MART-1 peptide; NFAT activity was measured using Steady-Glo. Computational methods included peptide-specific AVIB classifiers (with ProtBERT embeddings), a PPO-based mutation policy with a TCR autoencoder critic trained on 277M CDR3β sequences, post-filtering by k-mer clustering and Miyazawa–Jernigan heuristics, and structural/energy analyses: TCRmodel2 (AlphaFold2-based) complex prediction, DSMBind fine-tuned on TCR-pMHC structures, Rosetta FastRelax/backrub with InterfaceAnalyzer/ddG, and GROMACS MD (Amber ff14SB, GLYCAM06, TIP3P, PME; heating to 298.15 K; NPT equilibration with Langevin thermostat and Parrinello–Rahman barostat; LINCS constraints; 3 replicas×20 ns, total 120 ns per system) followed by MM/GBSA (gmx_MMPBSA, GB-neck2, internal dielectric 6.0, ionic strength 0.15 M).

summary: This study shows that hypoxia (1% O2) in multiple myeloma reduces BCMA expression and enhances a suppressive secretome, including increased release of small extracellular vesicles, which together diminish BCMA CAR T-cell signaling, cytotoxicity, and cytokine production. γ-Secretase inhibition with crenigacestat partially restores BCMA levels and CAR T-cell function, highlighting hypoxia-driven antigen loss and secretome-mediated suppression as barriers to BCMA-targeted immunotherapy.

summary: The study generated IL-15-armored CAR NK-92 cells targeting mesothelin (MSLN) and CD70 to attack pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) tumor cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), validating target expression in patient tumors and metastases. summary: This retrospective study molecularly profiled residual tumors from 138 triple‑negative breast cancer patients with extensive poor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, finding most cases were HER2‑ultralow/low and a high prevalence of TP53 mutations (94%), with additional alterations across PI3K/AKT/mTOR, DNA damage response, Wnt, and Notch pathways. summary: This article maps the principal ethical challenges in clinical CAR‑T therapy—non‑maleficence, uncertainty, shared decision‑making, distributive justice, and patient selection/prioritization—and argues that structured clinical ethics support is needed to address moral distress and improve fairness and patient‑centered care. It illustrates the use of moral case deliberation (MCD) via a detailed case of an older patient, and proposes integrating MCD into CAR‑T programs to guide difficult decisions and strengthen team resilience.

summary: This study shows that T cell–redirecting bispecific antibodies (blinatumomab) and CD19 CAR T cells kill malignant B cells via combined apoptotic and necroptotic mechanisms, with necroptosis dependent on RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL and independent of caspases, TNF, or TRAIL. summary: The study introduces NEO-AAV, a programmable extracellular vesicle–enveloped AAV platform created by a PH–ALG2–PKD12 fusion that actively recruits AAV capsids into EVs, improving capsid loading and resistance to neutralizing antibodies compared with passive EV-AAV. Displaying a CD7/CD3/CD28 tri-chimera enabled single-step activation and transduction of CD7+ T cells within human PBMCs and generated functional, transient CD19 CAR-T cells ex vivo.

HEK293FT cells were transfected (Lipofectamine 3000) with AAV packaging plasmids ± NEO constructs, cultured 72 h, and for conventional AAV the cells were subjected to three freeze–thaw cycles, Benzonase (50 U/mL), and detergent lysis, followed by PEG8000/NaCl precipitation, aqueous two-phase partitioning with PEG8000 and ammonium sulfate, dialysis into PBS, concentration, 0.22 µm sterile filtration, and storage at −80 °C. EV-AAV/NEO-AAV were collected from clarified supernatants (500 × g 5 min ×3; 2,000 × g 30 min; 0.45 µm filtration), pelleted by ultracentrifugation at 135,000 × g for 90 min at 4 °C, and further purified by qEVsingle 70 nm size-exclusion chromatography. For nano-flow cytometry, EVs were fixed by mixing with an equal volume of 8% paraformaldehyde (30 min RT), cleaned by SEC, permeabilized with 2× buffer on ice for 30 min, incubated with CaptureSelect AF647 Anti-AAVX at 37 °C for 30 min, cleaned by SEC, and analyzed on a NanoFCM. title: Persistent Campylobacter jejuni enterocolitis after CAR T-cell therapy in a patient with hypogammaglobulinemic follicular lymphoma

summary: This case report describes a 68-year-old man with hypogammaglobulinemia after CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy who developed persistent and disseminated Campylobacter jejuni enterocolitis and bacteremia, with clonal continuity confirmed by whole-genome sequencing. Five isolates underwent whole-genome sequencing at the Belgian National Reference Center for Campylobacter with virulence profiling via VFDB (v2025-10-10), resistance profiling via AMRFinderPlus (v2024-12-18.1), sequence typing via PubMLST, and SNP/cgMLST analyses, demonstrating clonal persistence (CC-443, ST-6522). summary: This narrative review evaluates intratumoral administration of blood-derived conventional dendritic cells (cDCs) to reactivate the cancer-immunity cycle in melanoma and other solid tumors, highlighting their superior cross-priming capacity compared with monocyte-derived DCs. summary: The study shows that upon engagement by NK cells, cancer cells rapidly remodel their actin cytoskeleton to concentrate HLA class I inhibitory ligands at the immunological synapse, thereby suppressing NK cell activation and cytotoxic polarization. For co-culture assays, NK and target cells were mixed (typically equal numbers or 2:1 NK:target) for 40–60 minutes at 37°C, followed by fixation with 4% PFA (15 min), permeabilization with 0.1% Triton X-100 (5 min), blocking (PBS with 5% BSA and 10% FBS), and immunostaining (e.g., HLA-A/B/C, HLA-C, granzyme B, γ-tubulin); conjugates were plated on poly-L-lysine–coated slides. Imaging was performed by confocal microscopy (Zeiss LSM880) and imaging flow cytometry (ImageStreamX Mark II) with defined synaptic/non-synaptic masks for quantitative analysis; no enzymatic tissue digestion was used.

summary: This study identifies DNA topoisomerase 2B (TOP2B) and the lamin B receptor (LBR) as coordinated regulators of genome–nuclear lamina (NL) interactions, where TOP2B predominantly binds inter-LAD regions to prevent their lamina association and LBR tethers LAD heterochromatin to the periphery. Depletion of TOP2B or LBR weakens LAD/iLAD partitioning, with co-depletion partially inverting LAD/iLAD states reminiscent of oncogene-induced senescence, while maintaining H3K9me3 heterochromatin and indicating a complementary TOP2B–LBR axis that organizes the genome at the NL.
summary_mandm: Human cell lines (RPE1, HCT116, K562, GM12878, HEK293T) were cultured in standard media; siRNA knockdowns (TOP1, TOP2A, TOP2B) were performed using Lipofectamine RNAiMAX with two transfections 48 h apart and assays 72 h after the second transfection; LBR knockout was generated via lentiviral delivery of inducible Cas9 and sgRNAs with 12 days G418 selection; pharmacological TOP2 inhibition used Merbarone (200 μM) or ICRF-193 (10–20 μM) for indicated times; bleomycin treatments were 3 h at 10 μM or 100 nM. title: Defining the Quality Attributes for Tumor-Infiltrating Lymphocyte Medicinal Products.
authors: Lievense, Justin J; Nijenhuis, Cynthia; Jedema, Inge; Jonker-Hoogerkamp, Arendien; Moyers, Justin T; Hamid, Omid; Beijnen, Jos H; Haanen, John B A G; Nuijen, Bastiaan

raw_affiliation: Department of Pharmacy & Pharmacology, Netherlands Cancer Institute-Antoni Van Leeuwenhoek Hospital, Amsterdam, The Netherlands.

summary: This review defines a quality target product profile and critical quality attributes for tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) medicinal products within a quality-by-design framework, mapping identity, purity, potency, dose, and stability to regulatory expectations. It links TIL mechanism-of-action to measurable functions (tumor recognition, cytotoxicity, homing, persistence), discusses suitable assays and limits, and proposes control strategies to support robust manufacturing and regulatory approval.
summary_mandm: Manufacturing is described as: excision of an autologous tumor lesion; tissue is either sliced into fragments for lymphocyte outgrowth or enzymatically digested (enzymes not specified) to release lymphocytes; pre-REP outgrowth occurs in IL-2-containing medium for several weeks; cells are then expanded in REP to billions of cells using OKT-3 (anti-CD3) stimulation with irradiated allogeneic feeder cells; products may be administered fresh or after cryopreservation and thawing. Potency/readout methods include TCR-based activation (CD3/CD28/CD137) followed by IFN-γ assays, co-culture with autologous tumor to measure activation (e.g., CD134/CD137, CD107a, IFN-γ, TNF-α) or direct killing (e.g., 51Cr, luciferase, LDH, live-cell analysis), and neoantigen-focused assays using pMHC multimers or APCs. Quality control methods include endotoxin testing (e.g., Endosafe), sterility testing with automated blood culture systems (e.g., BacTec; BaCT/Alert), and PCR-based mycoplasma testing; media components referenced include RPMI, AIM-V, and GlutaMAX; viability thresholds (e.g., ≥70%) and dose (e.g., ≥1–5×10^9 and often much higher) are emphasized. The review does not specify digestion enzymes, buffer compositions, temperatures, or exact incubation times beyond noting several-week pre-REP culture and standard REP practices.

cell_selection_method: CD137 (4-1BB) separation to enrich tumor-reactive T cells; CD8+ enrichment (method not specified); selection of confirmed tumor-reactive TIL cultures in the standard TIL protocol

summary: An international, multidisciplinary panel used a modified Delphi process to establish a consensus definition, classification framework, and minimum data elements (MDEs) for osteoradionecrosis of the jaw (ORNJ), aligned with SNOMED-CT and ISOO-MASCC-ASCO guidance. The study produced 10 consensus statements and 9 MDEs to standardize clinical and radiographic diagnosis, staging, and reporting, aiming to reduce ambiguity and enable interoperable data capture and analytics.
summary_mandm: A web-based modified Delphi methodology was conducted with 69 experts across four iterative rounds using REDCap and Qualtrics surveys, incorporating text-only and image-based case vignettes, review of existing classification systems, feature extraction, importance ratings, and iterative reclassification until consensus thresholds were met. The process aligned terminology with SNOMED-CT and MedDRA, assessed interrater reliability (Fleiss kappa), and focused on specifying clinical and imaging MDEs (e.g., probe-to-bone results, mucosal status, radiographic morphology, extent relative to alveolar bone) without involving patient specimens or laboratory digestion/preparation steps.

authors: Verhezen, Tias; Van Den Eynde, Astrid; Verstraelen, Peter; Gehrcken, Laura; Palmiotto, Gabriele; Lau, Ho Wa; De Vos, Winnok; Van der Heijden, Sanne; Brants, Louize; Melis, Jöran; Van Audenaerde, Jonas; Van Laere, Steven; Lardon, Filip; Deben, Christophe; Wouters, An; Smits, Evelien; De Waele, Jorrit
journal: BioRxiv : the Preprint Server for Biology
raw_affiliation: University of Antwerp
affiliation_notes: City not provided in the raw affiliation; country code BE converted to Belgium.
summary: The study shows that hypoxia impairs NK cell mitochondrial integrity and cytotoxicity, and that IL-15–armored CD70 CAR NK cells remain susceptible to this suppression. Pharmacologic inhibition or CRISPR-Cas9 knockout of DRP1 preserves mitochondrial content and membrane potential and restores cytotoxic function under hypoxia, enabling CD70-CAR-IL-15 DRP1KO NK cells to retain activity in low oxygen conditions.
summary_mandm: NK-92 cells were cultured in GlutaMAX α-MEM with 12.5% FBS, 12.5% horse serum, 2 mM L-glutamine, 1% P/S, and 150 U/mL IL-2 at 37 °C, 5% CO2; hypoxia was modeled at 1% O2 using H45 HEPA Hypoxystations (Don Whitley Scientific), typically for 48 h (24 h for RNA-seq). DRP1 knockout was generated by CRISPR-Cas9 RNP nucleofection of IL-2–pre-activated NK-92 (Lonza 4D Nucleofector) using three sgRNAs, validated by PCR and flow cytometry; CD70-CAR-IL-15 was introduced by in vitro–transcribed mRNA (T7 kit) electroporation (4 μg mRNA per 1×10^6 cells). For functional assays: co-cultures with K562 or Raji (5:1 E:T) ran 4 h; xCELLigence RTCA monitored longitudinal killing of adherent targets. Mitochondrial membrane potential and mtROS were measured by TMRM (100 nM, 30 min, 37 °C) and MitoSOX (1 μM, 30 min, 37 °C); viability staining used LIVE/DEAD reagents. For intracellular DRP1 staining, cells were fixed/permeabilized (eBioscience Foxp3 kit), blocked with 10% human serum, stained with anti–phospho-DRP1 (1 h, 4 °C) and Alexa Fluor 647 secondary (30 min). Confocal prep: cells were fixed in 2% PFA (10 min), cytospun (1500 rpm, 5 min), permeabilized with 1% Triton X-100 (5 min), stained overnight with anti-TOMM20 (1:250, 4 °C), followed by goat anti-mouse AF488 (1:500, 2 h, RT) plus CellMask (1:5000), and DAPI (5 μg/mL, 10 min). SCENITH used 2-DG (100 mM), oligomycin (1 μM), and puromycin (10 μg/mL) with standard calculations; Mdivi-1 was used to inhibit DRP1 during hypoxic culture.
sample_type: NK-92 NK cell line; tumor cell lines (HeLa; Panc-1; Raji; K562)
instrument: 4D Nucleofector (Lonza); H45 HEPA Hypoxystation (Don Whitley Scientific); Cytospin (ThermoFisher); xCELLigence RTCA (Agilent); NovoCyte Quanteon Flow Cytometer; CytoFLEX (Beckman Coulter); Nikon CSU-W1-SoRa spinning disk confocal
culture_medium: GlutaMAX α-MEM (Life Technologies) with 12.5% FBS; 12.5% horse serum; 2 mM L-glutamine; 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin; 150 U/mL recombinant IL-2
culture_timeframe: 48 h hypoxia; 24 h hypoxia prior to RNA-seq; 4 h co-culture cytotoxicity assays; 3-4 days per expansion cycle
transduction_method: mRNA electroporation (4D Nucleofector) for CD70-CAR-IL-15; CRISPR-Cas9 RNP nucleofection for DRP1 knockout

title: Dual targeting of CD155/TIGIT and PD-L1/PD-1 immune checkpoints potentiates NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity in medulloblastoma.

summary: The study identifies CD155 on medulloblastoma (MB) tumor cells and TIGIT on infiltrating immune cells, and shows that NK cell-derived interferon-γ can induce PD-L1 on MB cells. Dual checkpoint blockade with Tiragolumab (anti-TIGIT) and Durvalumab (anti-PD-L1) enhances NK cell activation and cytotoxicity against MB cell lines and PDX-derived organoids, proposing a translatable immunotherapeutic strategy for SHH and Group 3 MB.
summary_mandm: Human PBMCs from healthy donors were isolated by Ficoll-Paque gradient centrifugation, residual RBCs were lysed with ammonium lysis buffer, and NK cells were enriched by negative selection using MACS (Miltenyi human NK cell isolation kit with LS columns); NKs were activated for 2 h at 37 °C with IL-2 (1000 IU/mL) and IL-15 (50 ng/mL). MB cell lines (Daoy, HD-MB03, D283) were cultured in DMEM or RPMI-based media with serum; cells were detached with Trypsin/EDTA, stained (CFSE), and co-cultured with NKs for killing (48 h) or activation (5 h) assays with or without antibodies (Tiragolumab; Durvalumab). PDX-derived MB organoids (MED113FH, B062-008) were mechanically dissociated by gentle pipetting and passage through a 40 μm strainer to single cells, replated to reform 3D structures (24–48 h), then co-cultured with NKs ± antibodies for 48 h or subjected to live imaging; IHC used deparaffinization with EDTA antigen retrieval (TIGIT manual: EDTA pH 9.0, 100 °C 20 min) on an automated immunostainer. Additional assays included a Promega TIGIT/CD155 blockade bioassay (Jurkat TCR reporter + CD3/CD28 beads), intracellular IFN-γ staining (PFA fix; saponin), and qPCR.

title: Dysfunctional CD4 T cells in an oncovirus-specific TCR-transgenic in vivo model.
authors: Spitzer, Felicia S; Camps, Marcel G M; Britten, Cedrik M; Vloemans, Sandra; Van Zeeburg, Hester J T; Melief, Cornelis J M; Arakelian, Tsolere; Ossendorp, Ferry
raw_affiliation: Department of Immunology, Leiden University Medical Center, Leiden, The Netherlands. f.a.ossendorp@lumc.nl.
summary: The authors generate a Moloney MuLV envelope-specific CD4 TCR-transgenic mouse (MolT-II) whose CD4 T cells exhibit intrinsic dysfunction with impaired proliferation and elevated inhibitory checkpoint expression, attributed to cross-reactivity with an endogenous AKV env peptide expressed in the thymus. Antigen-specific peptide vaccination combined with triple checkpoint blockade (PD-L1, LAG-3, CTLA-4) restores MolT-II CD4 T-cell function and enhances tumor control, establishing MolT-II as a reversible in vivo model of CD4 T-cell dysfunction.
summary_mandm: MolT-II TCR-transgenic mice (C57BL/6 background) were generated by pronuclear co-injection of TCR α/β constructs and used alongside OT-II and TbiLuc crosses; spleen, lymph node, blood and thymus were processed to single-cell suspensions, with thymic stromal cells isolated by sequential enzymatic digestions (Collagenase IV and HEPES/2% FCS at 30°C for 15 min ×3; then Collagenase IV + Neutral Protease + DNase I at 37°C for 25 min ×5), EDTA (25 mM, 5 min, 37°C) rosette dissociation, and subsequent magnetic enrichment and FACS sorting of DCs and TEC subsets. For functional assays, D1 dendritic cells were peptide-loaded (0.05–10 μM; 4–5 h, 37°C), optionally matured with LPS (4 μg/ml, overnight), then co-cultured with splenocytes, with Brefeldin A added after 1 h; CFSE labeling used 5 μM CFSE for 10 min at 37°C and was quenched in IMDM + 10% FCS + antibiotics + L-glutamine + 25 μM β-mercaptoethanol. T-cell activation was induced with plate-coated anti-CD3ε (200 ng/ml or 1 μg/ml; 16 h) or soluble anti-CD3ε + anti-CD28 (1 μg/ml each; 5–7 h total), and in vivo with CpG-adjuvanted peptide vaccination; checkpoint blockade consisted of intraperitoneal anti-PD-L1, anti-LAG-3, and anti-CTLA-4 on days 0, 2, and 4. Imaging used IVIS with D-luciferin (localization) or CycLuc1 (NFAT-driven activation), and tumor protection employed envH + gagL peptides emulsified in IFA prior to RMA challenge.

instrument: AutoMACS (Miltenyi Biotec); FACSAria I cell sorter

authors: Akodad, Sanae; Goldman, Michel; Stevens, Hilde

summary: This policy review compares pre-approval early access pathways and timelines for innovative therapies across the US, EU, China, and Japan, showing how definitions of unmet medical need, clinical trial geography, regulatory accelerators, and fragmented early or expanded access mechanisms drive inequities in early patient treatment. It advocates adaptive licensing (live licenses), managed entry agreements, interoperable HTA and RWE/RWD integration, and internationally coordinated benefit–risk governance to deliver more timely and equitable access, especially for rare and high-burden diseases.

summary: This phase I/II clinical trial evaluated autologous tumor-infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapy plus nivolumab with or without pegylated IFNα in patients with checkpoint-refractory stage III/IV melanoma, showing that adding IFNα increased disease control from 11% to 42% with low toxicity. IFNα induced leukopenia/neutropenia correlated with response, while TIL product characteristics were similar across groups, supporting IFNα as a key supportive component in a non-lymphodepleting regimen.

title: Enabling next-generation engineered TCR-T therapies based on high-throughput TCR discovery from diagnostic tumor biopsies.
authors: Kuilman, Thomas; Schrikkema, Deborah S; Gadiot, Jules; Gomez-Eerland, Raquel; Bies, Laura; Walker, Julia; Spaapen, Robbert M; Kok, Hanna; Houg, Demi; Viyacheva, Milena; Claassen, Yvonne B; Saornil, Manuel; Krijgsman, Oscar; Stringer, Bas; Ding, Huiwen; Geleijnse, Anou; Meinema, Anne C; Weissbrich, Bianca; Lancee, Melissa; Engele, Carmen G; Sabatino, Marianna; Chen, Pei-Ling; Tsai, Kenneth Y; Mulé, James J; Sondak, Vernon K; Van Den Bulk, Jitske; De Miranda, Noel F; Jedema, Inge; Haanen, John G; Van Heijst, Jeroen W J; Schumacher, Ton N; Linnemann, Carsten; Bendle, Gavin M

summary: The study presents a high-throughput functional genetic screening platform that identifies tumor-specific TCRs directly from fresh-frozen diagnostic tumor biopsies (including non-viable core-needle biopsies) by screening combinatorial TCR libraries against multiplexed neoantigen libraries in autologous APCs. It demonstrates sensitive and specific discovery of both HLA class I- and II-restricted neoantigen-specific TCRs across melanoma, colorectal carcinoma, NSCLC, TNBC, SCC, and Merkel cell carcinoma, enabling next-generation individualized TCR-T therapies.
summary_mandm: Fresh-frozen (non-viable) tumor tissue was processed for gDNA/RNA using the Allprep DNA/RNA Mini Kit with mechanical disruption on a Qiagen TissueLyser, followed by WES/RNA-seq and multiplex PCR TCR profiling (MiLaboratories/MiXCR) to build synthetic, combinatorially assembled TCR libraries. B cells were isolated from PBMCs by magnetic selection (BioLegend MojoSort Pan B cell kit or Miltenyi CD20 MicroBeads with AutoMACS), activated on CD40L-expressing L cells, and cultured in RPMI (10% FCS, penicillin/streptomycin, sodium pyruvate, non-essential amino acids, GlutaMAX, 50 nM 2-mercaptoethanol) with IL-2 (100 IU/mL) then IL-4 (50 ng/mL) and IL-21 (50 ng/mL), followed by retroviral transduction with BCL-6/BCL-xL±CD40L, and later retroviral transduction of LAMP1-flanked TMG constructs with puromycin selection (1 μg/mL, 3–4 days). Peptide loading used Amaxa 4D Nucleofector electroporation (program Vero/DN100; SF buffer; ~2.5×10^7 cells/mL; peptide 40 mM in DMSO; rest 10 min; dilute 10× and incubate 4 h at 37°C), and HLA restriction employed CRISPR/Cas9 RNP B2M knockout (tracr/crRNA anneal 95°C 5 min; assemble with Cas9 15–20 min; electroporate with 4D Nucleofector; rest 10 min at 37°C; culture with IL-21). Jurkat TCR-KO CD8+ reporter cells were retrovirally transduced with TCR libraries (selected with blasticidin 4–6 μg/mL or puromycin 250 ng/mL), co-cultured 20–24 h with TMG-B cells, and sorted by FACS (CD69) or AutoMACS (dead-cell removal, CD20 depletion, CD62L fractionation, CD69-biotin/anti-biotin) before NGS-based TCR enrichment analysis; PMA/ionomycin served as activation control.

title: Engineering anti-BCMA CAR T cells for enhancing myeloma killing efficacy via apoptosis regulation.
authors: Kimman, Thomas; Cuenca, Marta; Tieland, Ralph G; Rockx-Brouwer, Dedeke; Janssen, Jasmijn; Motais, Benjamin; Slomp, Anne; Pleijte, Corine; Heijhuurs, Sabine; Meringa, Angelo D; Boschloo, Wendy; Bosma, Douwe M T; Kroos, Sanne; Lo Presti, Vania; Sluijter, Joost P G; Nierkens, Stefan; Bovenschen, Niels; Kuball, Jürgen; Van Mil, Alain; Minnema, Monique C; Sebestyén, Zsolt; Peperzak, Victor
raw_affiliation: Center for Translational Immunology, University Medical Center Utrecht, Utrecht, Netherlands. v.peperzak@umcutrecht.nl.

summary: The study engineers anti-BCMA CAR T cells that carry a granzyme B–NOXA fusion to locally deliver the pro-apoptotic NOXA into multiple myeloma cells, thereby overcoming MCL-1–mediated apoptosis resistance and enhancing tumor killing. These NOXA-armed CAR T cells improved in vitro cytotoxicity and delayed tumor growth in xenograft models without detectable toxicity to bystander bone marrow cells or cardiomyocytes, suggesting a generalizable strategy to boost CAR T efficacy.
summary_mandm: Human PBMCs (from buffy coats) were isolated by Ficoll-Paque, preactivated with anti-CD3 (OKT3, 30 ng/mL) and IL-2 (50 IU/mL), retrovirally transduced (Phoenix-Ampho; polybrene 6 μg/mL) with anti-BCMA (or anti-CD19) CARs, selected with geneticin (80 μg/mL), and expanded using a rapid expansion protocol with irradiated feeder PBMCs/LCL, OKT3 (30 ng/mL), IL-2 (50 U/mL), IL-15 (5 ng/mL), and PHA-L (1 μg/mL). For arming, lentiviral vectors encoding granzyme B–cargo–T2A–eGFP (cargo: mScarlet, mNeonGreen, or NOXA/iNOXA) were produced (CalPhos transfection), viral supernatants were filtered, ultracentrifuged (20,000 × g, 2 h), resuspended in StemMACS, and used to transduce CAR T cells; eGFP+ cells were sorted and expanded. Primary MM bone marrow mononuclear cells (frozen) were thawed, cultured with IL-6 (100 ng/mL) and APRIL (100 ng/mL), and in some assays pretreated with MCL-1 inhibitor S63845 (100 nM) for 48 h prior to 24 h CAR T co-culture; co-culture viability was measured by flow cytometry (TO-PRO-3, DiOC6(3)). For exogenous NOXA delivery, streptolysin O (15 ng/mL; activated with 10 mM DTT) and synthetic NOXA/NOXA-TAMRA were incubated with target cells for 30 min at 37 °C before serum quenching; apoptosis was assessed 24 h later. hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes were generated by a GiWi protocol (CHIR99021 4 μM for 48 h, then Wnt-C59 2 μM; sequential heparin and insulin media), and metabolic activity (alamarBlue) and beating were assessed after exposure to MCL-1i, exogenous NOXA, or co-culture with NOXA3X CAR T plus MM cells.
sample_type: PBMC; bone marrow mononuclear cells; multiple myeloma cells; iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes
miltenyi_product: Lentiviral particles were produced by transient transfection of the lentiviral vector and the packaging plasmids pRSV-Rev, pMDLg/ pRRE, and pMD2-VSV-G to HEK293T cells using the CalPhos Mammalian Transfection Kit (Clontech Laboratories). Viral supernatants were filtered through 0.45 μm low-protein-binding filters (Sarstedt), concentrated by ultracentrifugation at 20,000 × g for 2 h, resuspended in StemMACS (Miltenyi Biotec), and stored at −80 °C.

summary: This prospective single-center feasibility study evaluated whether exhaled breath volatile organic compound (VOC) patterns captured by an electronic nose (Aeonose) before treatment can predict lack of clinical benefit from first-line immune checkpoint inhibitors in patients with metastatic melanoma. summary: This review discusses the limitations of 2D co-culture systems for evaluating CAR-T cell efficacy in solid tumors and highlights next-generation 3D models—spheroids, organoids, organ-on-chip, and bioprinting—as more physiologically relevant platforms. It outlines strategies to generate and interrogate these models, compares them with murine in vivo studies, and summarizes advances in CAR-T engineering and delivery to better address tumor microenvironment barriers.

CAR-T cells are added during aggregation to study activation/killing or after spheroid/organoid formation to study infiltration and cytotoxicity; analysis includes confocal/live-cell imaging, flow cytometry after dissociation, ELISA (IL-2, IFN-γ, TNF-α), viability assays, and histology. summary: This consensus guidance reviews evidence and proposes criteria for using autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (AHSCT) and emerging cellular therapies (such as CD19 CAR-T) in juvenile systemic sclerosis (jSSc), adapting adult SSc criteria to pediatric contexts. It integrates adult and pediatric data, survey results, and a multidisciplinary nominal group process to prioritize disease progression and organ involvement (skin, lung, heart, muscle) in selecting jSSc candidates, and presents preliminary clinical experience from a pediatric center demonstrating feasibility and safety of AHSCT.
summary_mandm: In the pediatric cohort described, stem cells were mobilized with cyclophosphamide and filgrastim (G-CSF), collected via apheresis, and CD34+ selected; the autologous peripheral blood stem cell grafts were cryopreserved and later infused. summary: This plenary session summary highlights translational advances in autoimmune vasculitis, especially ANCA-associated vasculitis, spanning microbiome modulation (resistant starch/acetate), Treg-mediated suppression, MPO-specific B cell biology, CD19 CAR-T therapy in murine models, IL-17 pathway targeting in GCA, type I interferon signatures, and nuclear-penetrating antibodies (DX-1/DX-3) that reduce NETs and renal injury. Collectively, these studies suggest promising preclinical avenues toward targeted, potentially personalized therapies that may achieve drug-free remission while preserving host defense.

Human MPO-specific B cells were identified by a flow cytometry-based approach, with stimulated B-cell cultures producing MPO-IgM; temporal artery biopsies were cultured ex vivo with secukinumab, IL-17, and IFN-γ; kidney transcriptomics and PBMC analyses assessed type I interferon signatures and serum IFNα. CD19 CAR-T cells were administered in a murine MPO-AAV model and monitored for migration/persistence and B-cell depletion; stimulated human neutrophils were treated with Deoxy Mab DX-1/DX-3 to assess NET formation, with parallel in vivo evaluation in mice. summary: The study shows that loss of DOT1L in mature mouse CD8 T cells, via inducible knockout or selective inhibition, reduces TCR/CD8 surface levels yet reprograms cells toward an innate-like, effector-memory state with increased granzymes and perforin, thereby enhancing antigen-specific cytotoxicity in vitro without compromising proliferation, viability, or in vivo tumor control. authors: Wang, Daisong; Lim, Sangho; Van de Wetering, Willine J; Lopez-Iglesias, Carmen; Okura, Yuu; Teranishi-Ikawa, Yuri; Mizoroki, Akihiko; Spoelstra, Willem Kasper; Dayton, Talya; Van Son, Gijs J F; Pronk, Apollo; Smakman, Niels; Gonera-De Jong, Gieneke B C; Withoff, Sebo; Jonkers, Iris H; Van Zon, Jeroen S; Tans, Sander J; Peters, Peter J; Van Es, Johan H; Clevers, Hans

summary: This study establishes a human intestinal organoid model that robustly differentiates M cells and shows they constitutively express MHC-II, share dendritic cell-like programs, and directly present antigens. Human M cells process and deamidate gliadin via TGM2 and activate HLA-DQ2.5–restricted T cells, implicating M cells as antigen-presenting cells in celiac disease, with development requiring RANKL/CSF2 and transcription factors SPIB and RUNX2.
summary_mandm: Human intestinal organoids were cultured in BME droplets in OCHIO medium and differentiated to M cells using M cell medium (OCHIO + 100 ng/ml RANKL, 20 ng/ml TNF, 0.1 μM retinoic acid) for 5–8 days; ALI monolayers were generated on BME-coated transwells with basolateral M cell medium for 6–8 days. Organoids were released from BME with ice-cold Corning Cell Recovery Solution, dissociated with TrypLE Express (37°C, 6–8 min) and gentle pipetting, filtered through 40 μm strainers, or mechanically sheared before co-culture; apical-out polarity was achieved by overnight suspension culture in M cell medium + 3 μM CHIR99021 after matrix removal. Primary human terminal ileum/Peyer’s patches were microdissected and digested in adDMEM/F12 with 1 mg/ml collagenase and 5 mM EDTA for 30 min at 37°C with intermittent shaking, then passed through 100 μm strainers; gliadin was processed by pepsin (2 mg/ml, 2 h, 37°C, 0.2 N HCl), neutralized to pH 7.4, treated with trypsin (4 h, 37°C), heat-inactivated (100°C, 30 min), optionally deamidated with TGM2 (1 mg/ml in PBS + 1 mM CaCl2, 2 h, 37°C) and freeze-dried. Cells were FACS-sorted (DAPI− live; markers ICAM2, GP2, MHC-II) for scRNA-seq (SORT-seq) or co-culture; IFNγ treatments were 48 h; antigen incubation prior to co-culture was 5 h; T-cell co-cultures were overnight or 24 h, with proliferation readouts at 5 days.
